study: Posthoc, unprespecified candidate follow-up on frozen synthetic corpus.

candidate_text.review: For dependency-update diffs, classify an evidence gap or unknown as a gap/risk, not a speculative confirmed defect. Assess correctness in mixed diffs as well as package compatibility.
guide: Classify each consumer separately: a queued/pending/skipped job is unexercised, not blocked, unless evidence identifies its failed or denied prerequisite. Do not copy an aggregate row’s state to every consumer.

Record a prerequisite gap once in the consumer table rather than duplicating it as a defect. A bounded advisory caveat must not erase an otherwise successful tested scenario or create an advisory finding without evidence.

configuration.calls: Fresh independent evaluators; no repeats; same 15 corpus inputs; no skill tool invocation in any arm.
limits: Posthoc candidate follow-up, not prespecified uplift; original oracle retained only for scoring and never shown to evaluators.
Inherited instructions cannot be removed; original system/repository guidance may contaminate baselines.
Candidate evidence arm is guide-loaded only, not skill-invoked.
Matched requested defaults do not verify concrete model/settings.

oracle.rubric: Targets are actionable supported findings or bounded evidence gaps, not necessarily product bugs. TP/miss use adjudicated finding-to-target matches; false positives are definite unsupported defect/test demands; unsupported claims include safety/execution assertions. Format omissions alone are not substantive FP. Evidence fidelity denominators include only assessable explicit citations/head/execution statements. Allowed row states describe dominant condition, not exhaustive consumer states.

targets.host-gap: minimum host and Node runtime need actual verification; types alone not proof

targets.compile-lint-gap: coupled major toolchain needs compile/lint/peer evidence

targets.restore-blocked: feed auth prerequisite blockage, not incompatibility

targets.lock-drift: current-head compiler generated actual lock drift

targets.policy-unknown: allow-list not confirmed; no confirmed violation

targets.resolution-mismatch: selector/lock coherence discrepancy; no affected advisory established

targets.traversal: B decoded traversal violates stated scope; A encoded package scope is allowed

targets.redis-skipped: Redis selected but skipped, template actually exercised

The required compile, lint, and extension-host validation is a coverage gap because none of those scenarios ran.

The TypeScript, ESLint, and typescript-eslint major upgrades have no supplied migration or peer-compatibility evidence, and the selected extension job remains pending; toolchain compatibility is therefore unverified, not a confirmed failure.
There is no executed compile, lint, or installation result to validate the changed toolchain.
H1 restore validation is blocked by an HTTP 401 from the unchanged approved feed; this is not evidence of a package compile defect, but build and test behavior remain unverified.
The generated workflow lock file is stale for compiler 0.51: compiling changed its timeout from 10 to 15 minutes, while the committed lock file was unchanged.

scoring_notes.finding_emission: Unique finding-to-target matches; table-only explicit target recognition is reported separately.
scoring_notes.false_positive: Zero unsupported substantive defect findings; non-target bounded evidence gaps are separately counted.
scoring_notes.taxonomy: Case aggregate state and each consumer execution state are separate metrics. Redis blocked in candidate-review is the only consumer-state taxonomy error; 401-linked dependent work can be blocked because the prerequisite failure is explicitly evidenced.
scoring_notes.duplicate: No repeated substantive defect findings. Supported ancillary gap findings are counted as non-target observations, not false positives.
